description: Shared hook helpers: session-id sanitising, transcript/cwd path validation, stdin parsing, stdout response, project-root resolution and the error log. Test data only. `expect` holds what the tests assert, as checks [{path, op, value}] against {"result": <return value>} (or {"parsed": ...} for stdout) or as a sentence where the test asserts a property. Path functions are platform dependent: `computed_win32` was computed on Windows with Python 3.13; `computed_posix_simulated` by running the same function with posixpath in place of os.path. `test_runs_on` marks tests that assert only on one platform. {TMP} is an absolute directory (forward slashes); in log cases it is a fresh empty dir.

sources.identical_on: master (module and tests have no diff)

regexes.name: _SESSION_ID_RE
regexes.note: Python `$` also matches just before a final '\n', so 'abc\n' is accepted (see probe.trailing_newline_accepted). Rust `$` without (?m) matches only at the end of the text. Recommended: keep the Rust form and reject the trailing newline.

regexes.name: _WINDOWS_DEVICE_RE
regexes.used_with: re.match on the session id and on os.path.basename(cwd)
regexes.note: Same trailing-newline difference. `.` excludes '\n' in both engines.

rules.sanitize_session_id: '' -> ''; len > 128 -> ''; not matching _SESSION_ID_RE -> ''; matching _WINDOWS_DEVICE_RE -> ''; else unchanged.
rules.validate_transcript_path: '' -> ''; contains '..' anywhere -> ''; not os.path.isabs -> ''; else unchanged.
rules.validate_cwd: '' -> ''; len > 4096 -> ''; contains '..' -> ''; not os.path.isabs -> ''; basename non-empty and matching _WINDOWS_DEVICE_RE -> ''; else unchanged. No I/O.
rules.read_stdin: raw = sys.stdin.read(524288) (characters); empty or whitespace-only -> {}; json.loads; not an object -> {}; any exception -> {}.
rules.write_stdout_response: json.dump({'continue': True, 'suppressOutput': True}) + '\n', flush; exceptions swallowed.
rules._resolve_log_dir: $SPATIAL_MEMORY_MEMORY_PATH if non-empty; else os.path.join(cwd, '.spatial-memory') if cwd; else '' (no logging).
log_hook_error: If hook-errors.log exists and its size > 1048576 bytes: delete hook-errors.log.1 if present, rename the log to hook-errors.log.1 (OSError ignored).

Append '[%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ] {hook_name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\n' (UTC) in text mode, UTF-8 (CRLF on Windows, so the size threshold counts the CR bytes there). computed_files show log text with CRLF normalised to LF and timestamps as {TIMESTAMP}; `crlf` and `size_bytes_win32` record the raw Windows file.
rules.platform: Python 3.13 on Windows: ntpath.isabs('/x') and isabs('\\x') are False (no drive); 'C:/x', 'C:\\x' and UNC paths are absolute; 'C:x' is not.

validate_cwd_cases.name: rejects_windows_device
validate_cwd_cases.notes: The test asserts only when sys.platform == 'win32'.

validate_cwd_cases.name: valid_unix_path
validate_cwd_cases.notes: The test asserts only when sys.platform != 'win32'. On Windows (Python 3.13) the value is rejected because it has no drive (see computed_win32).

read_stdin_cases.name: large_stdin_truncated
read_stdin_cases.notes: The test asserts `result == {} or isinstance(result, dict)` (any dict). Reading stops after 524288 characters, which cuts the string, so the JSON is invalid and the result is {}.

write_stdout_response_cases.name: writes_valid_json
write_stdout_response_cases.notes: json.dump default separators, then '\n', then flush. On a Windows text-mode pipe the newline becomes CRLF.

sanitization_integration_cases.name: malicious_session_id_rejected_by_load_state
sanitization_integration_cases.notes: Computed with SPATIAL_MEMORY_MEMORY_PATH set to an empty scratch dir (the test does not set it; the sanitised id is empty so no file is read).

log_hook_error_cases.name: never_raises
log_hook_error_cases.notes: No SPATIAL_MEMORY_MEMORY_PATH and no cwd: _resolve_log_dir returns '' and nothing is written.

sanitize_session_id.name: probe.trailing_newline_accepted
sanitize_session_id.notes: Python quirk: re.match with '$' also matches before a final '\n', so 'abc\n' is returned unchanged and would become a file name. Rust `^...$` (no multi-line flag) rejects it. Recommended Rust behaviour: reject.

sanitize_session_id.name: probe.device_with_trailing_newline
sanitize_session_id.notes: Passes the charset regex (trailing-newline quirk) and is then rejected by the device regex (same quirk).

validate_transcript_path.name: probe.posix_root_path
validate_transcript_path.notes: Python 3.13 ntpath.isabs('/tmp/t.jsonl') is False (rooted but no drive), so Windows rejects it. Earlier Pythons returned True.

validate_transcript_path.name: probe.double_dot_inside_name
validate_transcript_path.notes: Substring check: any '..' rejects, even inside a file name.

validate_cwd.name: probe.length_4096_ok
validate_cwd.notes: POSIX-style absolute path; rejected on Windows only because it has no drive.

validate_cwd.name: probe.length_4096_ok_drive
validate_cwd.notes: Drive-style absolute path of exactly 4096 characters.

validate_cwd.name: probe.device_trailing_separator
validate_cwd.notes: basename of a path ending in a separator is '' so the device check is skipped.

read_stdin.name: probe.limit_counts_characters_not_bytes
read_stdin.notes: sys.stdin is a text stream; read(524288) counts decoded characters, so 1048565 bytes of UTF-8 input still parse. The v2 dispatcher reads stdin differently (see event_aliases.json and hook_payloads).

read_stdin.name: probe.nan_accepted
read_stdin.notes: Python json accepts NaN/Infinity; serde_json does not.

read_stdin.name: probe.lone_surrogate_escape
read_stdin.notes: Python json accepts a lone surrogate escape; serde_json rejects it.

read_stdin.name: probe.control_char_prefix
read_stdin.notes: strip() sees non-empty text; json.loads rejects \x1c -> {}.

log_hook_error.name: probe.cwd_param_used_without_env
log_hook_error.notes: Log path is os.path.join(cwd, '.spatial-memory', 'hook-errors.log'); the directory is created.

log_hook_error.name: probe.keyerror_message_quoted
log_hook_error.notes: str(KeyError('x')) is "'x'" (Python repr of the key).

log_hook_error.name: probe.empty_message
log_hook_error.notes: Line ends with ': ' and no message.

log_hook_error.name: probe.multiline_message
log_hook_error.notes: The message is written raw, so the second physical line has no timestamp prefix.

log_hook_error.name: probe.oserror_errno_format

lines: [{TIMESTAMP}] H: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory

log_hook_error.notes: Python turns OSError(2, msg) into FileNotFoundError and formats it as '[Errno 2] msg'; the logged type name is the subclass.

log_hook_error.name: probe.exception_subclass_name_only

computed_exc.str: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte

lines: [{TIMESTAMP}] H: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte

log_hook_error.notes: Only type(exc).__name__ is written (no module path); the message is Python's str(exc).
